data.narrative:
Enigma is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jonathan Jacobi and Gal Niv, both former Unit 8200 operatives with prior tenures at Microsoft and Check Point. The company has raised $71M to date. The applicable comp universe spans 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set—1 same-stage company, 0 adjacent-stage peers, and 0 similar-tier comparables—precludes a robust peer-median approach.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method here. Using total raised ($71M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next financing stage yields $178M. This reflects observed progression patterns in frontier-tech funding without relying on scant peer comparables. The method's strength lies in its grounding in realized capital velocity; its limitation is sensitivity to the multiplier assumption and the lack of company-specific margin or revenue data to stress-test the projection.

The triangulated range, supported by this single method, spans $151M (low) to $204M (high), with a median of $178M. Key uncertainties center on the appropriate stage-progression multiplier for this particular cohort and the absence of financial performance data to calibrate the valuation further. A future peer-median approach may become viable as additional same-stage robotics companies reach funding milestones.
